title: Bone graft for a cleft in the gum: the three stages

plate: false tooth you can take out

sentences: This is the upper jaw of a child, about 9 to 10 years old.
The child was born with a split in the lip, gum and roof of the mouth on the left, called a cleft.
Under the pink gum, there is a gap in the bone that holds the teeth.
Its medical name is the alveolar cleft.
The small tooth next to the left front tooth never grew.
About half of children with a cleft do not have this tooth.
High in the bone, the adult eye tooth waits to come down.
It needs bone to grow into.
At about 8 to 11 years old, a surgeon fills the gap with bone, most often from the hip.
This is a bone graft.
It joins the jaw, holds up the teeth and nose, and closes any hole into the nose.
This is the same jaw, about 2 to 3 years after the bone graft.
The child is now about 12 to 13 years old.
Bone now joins the two parts of the upper jaw.
The eye tooth came down through the new bone into the row of teeth.
Some eye teeth get stuck and need a small operation.
Fixed braces line up the teeth.
Almost everyone who has this graft needs them.
A false tooth on the wire fills the gap where the small tooth never grew.
Soon after the operation, the gum healed over the graft.
If the wound opens early on, you can lose some of the graft.
An X-ray at about 3 to 6 months shows how well the new bone has taken.
Your hip can be sore for a while.
In one study, children went back to school about 2 weeks after surgery.
This is the same jaw in the later teens.
The braces are off.
Bone holds the teeth where the gap was.
Growth has stopped, so your dentist can now fill the gap for good.
There are three main ways.
An implant is a small post in the bone with a false tooth on top.
A bridge is a false tooth with one wing glued to the tooth next to it.
Or a plate you can take out holds a false tooth.
Some teams close the space instead.
Braces move the eye tooth into the gap, and the dentist reshapes it.
Your cleft team will help you choose.
